profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer
profile.summary: As an emerging technology professional, I love the challenges of working within a dynamic and fast paced environment. My resourcefulness and unwavering willingness to learn has shaped my ability to adapt quickly, work efficiently, and to think creatively. I believe in the agile methodology and enjoy building products and finding solutions that emphasize the user experience. Ultimately, I’m looking for a place where I can learn and grow as an individual, as a developer, and as a leader.

positions.title: Applications Business Analyst–Academic Advising Technology
positions.description: As an Applications Business Analyst, I work closely with technical staff and functional leads in academic advising to implement solutions that support the University's Graduations Success Initiative. I analyze, design, and create specifications for new PeopleSoft features, and work with developers to implement, test, and document changes before rolling them out to production. Since the main product I support (e_Advisor) is in it's maintenance phase of the life cycle, I'm also responsible for troubleshooting/testing any application bugs that may arise. As the SME, I also work with the training team to make sure they're up to date on new features and enhancements. I also spend much of my time building queries and reports that involve academic advising data. For the last year, I've been working with the University's BI team to model academic advising data for future reporting needs in Oracle BI.

positions.title: Assistant to the Director–School of Computing & Information Sciences
positions.description: As the Assistant to the Director of SCIS at FIU, I was responsible for handling day-to-day administrative tasks on behalf of the Director. I routed his phone calls, drafted his emails/memos/correspondence, organized his meetings, arranged his travel, etc. I proofread and edited manuscripts and research papers for the Director and for his PhD students. I strengthened my communication and interpersonal skills by becoming his official interface with the university. The School often hosted research conferences in the Miami area, so I also had the opportunity to serve on local arrangement committees for top-tier conferences! In this role, I was responsible for negotiating contract rates with local hotels, hiring caterers, planning receptions, handling A/V needs for the sessions, etc.

positions.title: Emerging Leaders Intern–Information Technology
positions.description: As a summer a Intern for RCCL, I worked with a talented team of analysts, project managers, and developers to test the next phase of the Choice Air project, a web application for cruise customers to purchase flights at discounted rates. I learned XML in order to validate the communications between the company's legacy reservation system and it's associated airfare booking site. Additionally, I was responsible for creating and testing against cases involving cruise/airfare promotions, and reporting anomalies in the company's QA management system (HP Quality Center).

projects.title: T-Shirt Order Form, Prototype Development
projects.description: A prototype I developed using Axure RP for my human computer interactions course.

projects.description: An angular app that we developed as part of my software engineering course.
